title: IASC-ASCE SHM benchmark 4-storey braced frame, 120DOF model, damage (ii): no 1st/3rd-storey braces

source.citation: Johnson, Lam, Katafygiotis, Beck (2004). Phase I IASC-ASCE Structural Health Monitoring Benchmark Problem Using Simulated Data. J. Eng. Mech. 130(1):3-15.
source.where: Report_bldg_shm_ana1.pdf Table 1 (members) and Table 2 (natural frequencies, 120DOF lumped mass); model DataGen/cal_model.m in Files_bldg_shm_ana1.zip, NEES database doi:10.4231/D3Q52FC7T
source.independence: Published by the benchmark authors from their own MATLAB model (HKUST code); not computed by stabileo or by this generator.

modelling: Columns/beams Euler-Bernoulli 3D frames; columns oriented by cal_model's k-nodes (localY = k - i), beams with local y horizontal (see below); braces are trusses; G = E/2.6.
Rigid floors: XY diaphragm on each floor's centre node (cal_model's reference point); the diaphragm ties every slave's rz to the master, as cal_model's T does.
Member masses lumped (mbar*L/2 per end, 3 translations; 967.213 kg above the base) and floor panel masses (x, y, theta only) carried by mass-only truss stubs; see generator docstring.
Member torsional rotary inertia (Io/A*mbar*L/2 about each member axis) carried by rotary-inertia frame stubs (torsion mass only).
Floor beams oriented with the strong axis in vertical bending (paper p. 10: Table 2 is from the HKUST code with corrected floor-beam orientation; the archived cal_model.m has the old one).
Damaged braces removed (cal_model sets their E to 0 and keeps their mass).
